reason: FEASIBILITY: survives. It is a desk rule with no new pipeline code. The E[D+] closed form plus a 20k-draw Monte Carlo runs in <1 min of laptop python on existing CSVs (l5_per_video_confirmation_vs_exp39.csv and l6_per_video_confirmation_vs_ef.csv exist). Every candidate component is already a composable builder patch: tools/build_probe_kernel.py documents that edgefilter, stitch, leafprune, divinsert and coordhead compose in any order, and they are exact no-ops when off. exp48-exp51 are built, and one kernel costs about 1,713 s of GPU out of ~20 h left. It adds at most 1-2 probe slots out of ~25 before the deadline. It touches no post-processing step, so it cannot conflict with relink, gap closing, safe divisions, leaf prune, DN insertion or the edge filter. Weak points that do not refute it: (1) SCORING LATENCY is 7.5-10+ h, not 3-6 h. Probe 28 took ~7.5 h, and probes 29/30 (submitted 09:41 UTC) were still PENDING at ~19:30 UTC. The chain is sequential: probe 29 result -> F1 composition exp48+ef (never built as one kernel; exp49 = exp39+ef) -> +coordhead probe -> F2 bundle probe. That is 3 serial scoring rounds before 29 Sep 20:00, which fits with about 1 day of slack only if each is submitted the same day the previous one scores. (2) THE CANDIDATE SET IS THIN. The div-cap research verdict is 'do NOT raise the cap' (0 TP / 2 FP beyond cap 4), and leaf prune and DN insertion are already in exp48. The real F2 differentiators are only {edge filter toggle, stitch, coordhead toggle}. (3) Stitch was lab-measured only ON TOP of the edge filter; it is placed after the edgefilter call. If probe 29 loses and ef is dropped, stitch's per-embryo screen (ii) needs a new replay run, which contradicts the refined test's 'no replay runs'. The Kaggle CPU lab port is paused, so that run falls back to the laptop lab at Idle priority. (4) The replay cache holds FIXED integer detector nodes and edge probabilities, so coordhead cannot be lab-screened. Once F1 contains coordhead, every lab delta used in screen (ii) was measured on a different base. Coordhead moves 143k peaks, changes 2.9% of final nodes and changes edge probabilities through the trilinear gather, which changes the set of edges the network never scored that ef targets. Only the bundle's public probe covers that interaction. (5) With ef in both finals, the only F2 differentiator is stitch. By the refined formula its s is ~0.0018 (it barely passes the s >= 0.0015 screen), and E[D+] at mu 0 is ~0.0007 vs ~0.0002 for a near-copy. So the premium sits exactly at the +0.0005 success threshold, and the rule's own fallback applies. (6) Kaggle final ticking is manual in the UI: the user must tick both finals by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC, or Kaggle auto-picks the two best public submissions. None of these makes it infeasible.
fix_if_any: 1) Make the schedule explicit, assuming 8-10 h scoring latency: build exp52 = exp48 + ef (+ stitch variant) as soon as probe 29 scores, not after. Submit the coordhead-on-final-base and F2-bundle kernels by 27 Sep 12:00 UTC at the latest, not 28 Sep 12:00, so a failed or late score still leaves one retry. 2) Replace 'no replay runs' with ONE replay run of the exact non-coordhead F1 and F2 configs (exp48 + ef +/- stitch, or exp48 + stitch if ef is dropped) under the selection->confirmation per-embryo screen. Run it on the Kaggle CPU lab or the laptop lab at Idle, since stitch is only measured on the ef base. 3) State that coordhead's interaction with the other components is screened ONLY by the public floor (bundle public >= F1 - 0.003). Do not claim a lab screen for it. Apply the J-vs-multiplier screen to coordhead too: its node drop of -2.9% gives a multiplier share of ~37%, over the 30% limit. If coordhead fails that screen, it becomes the natural high-sigma F2 differentiator instead of an F1 component. 4) Drop 'DaughterNet cap c*' from the candidate list (its own research refuted raising the cap). Replace it with the J-invariant fork-removal rule (fork-midpoint filter) only if that rule passes its own lab gate. 5) Put a manual tick of both finals in the 29 Sep checklist and verify it by reading the submissions page.
realistic_public_gain: 0 on the public LB by construction: this rule selects finals and never changes a submission's public score. Expected private-rank value is ~+0.0005..+0.0015 over auto-picking the two best public submissions. It is largest (~+0.001-0.002) if probe 29 ties and ef becomes the F2 differentiator, and ~+0.0005 (at threshold) if ef wins and stitch is the only differentiator. Cost: 1-2 probe slots and ~1 GPU h.
